svg.text: Wiring: FFB Pedal PCB V8 with external hardware brake resistor
PSU → SR5100 → MOSFET board (Diy_Hardware_BrakeResistor) → servo · PCB V8 → load cell + servo signals
also supplies the PCB with 5 V
one servo + one PCB V8 per pedal

g.text: = same DC IN screw terminal (PSU and servo wires clamped together)
• PCB V8 has no 36 V input. The USB-C port of the ESP32-S3 supplies the PCB with 5 V and connects the pedal to the PC (SimHub). The servo supply never passes through the PCB.
• Servo supply: PSU +V → SR5100 (band towards the module) → DC IN + → servo +Vdc; PSU −V → DC IN − → servo GND. Further pedals: clamp their servo wires into the same DC IN terminals.
• Servo signals: P± → PUL±, D± → DIR±, A± → ALM±. RS232 is crossed: board RX → servo TX, board TX → servo RX, GND → GND.
• Load cell: E+ → 5V, E− → G, shield → second G, S+ → +, S− → −. Wire colours differ between load cells, check the datasheet. If the force reads inverted, swap + and −.
• Zener: band to DC IN +. Keep the PSU at ≤ 37 V, otherwise the brake resistor stays switched on permanently.
• SimHub plugin: set Regen handling to “Hardware brake resistor circuit only”. Switch on the servo supply before connecting the PCB.
